bear.narrative: The market does not recover to mid-cycle. Fed by the oversupply the producers' association describes [S9, F41], the gross margin stays at the Q2-Q3 2026 exit run-rate of about 1 per cent rather than converging to the FY2025 witnessed level, so revenue growth is three points lower and the gross margin three points lower than base in every year. Operating cost carries the same witnessed rent as the base case, and the base case itself charges the annualised rent the nine months actually show rather than the two months booked: selling and administrative expense of Rp11.42bn in nine months [S10, F50, F51] includes rent from 29 July only, budgeted opex for FY2026E of Rp15.23bn assumes an unchanged run-rate, and from FY2027E we add Rp1.4bn a year for the missing ten months, so both the base and the bear pay for the lease [S8, F35]. The market-yield rent is disclosed as the upper end of a range in section 5 rather than shocked here, because the lease terms are not in the public material and charging it on one side only would be an unsourced asymmetry. Refinancing the debt that falls due against a current ratio of 0.98 costs two points more [S0].

bull.narrative: The government's supply control bites - early culling of parent stock at 50-55 weeks against the 65-week laying life the association itself states [S9, F41] - and the farm-gate live-bird price recovers above cost of production, with the chick line compounding from the evidence already in the accounts: day-old-chick sales rose 86.25 per cent year on year to Rp143.89bn and are now 70.78 per cent of revenue [S3, F23], the price of a day-old chick is already above Rp8,800 a bird [S7, F34], and the sale and leaseback retired bank debt so that net debt fell from Rp40.2bn at FY2025 to Rp25.5bn at 30 September [S0, S10, F58-F61]. Revenue growth is three points higher and the gross margin three points higher than base in every year: on the base path that is a realised margin of eight to nine and a half per cent at mid-cycle, above the 7.5 per cent of FY2022 and the 6.8 per cent of FY2023 [S0, S6] but well below the 16.6 per cent the first quarter of 2026 actually earned on Rp9.39bn of gross profit over Rp56.39bn of sales [S0]. The bull is a full peak-cycle recovery, not an extrapolation of the March spike. Operating cost carries the same witnessed rent as the base case: there is no source for a rent reduction, so the bull does not collect one. The cost of debt is two points lower as the balance sheet is repaired.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the nine-month actual, not on a forecast: sales of Rp203.28bn to September 2026 against Rp225.42bn a year earlier, down 9.82 per cent [S3, F19, F43]. The fourth quarter of 2025 contributed Rp41.6bn (FY2025 sales of Rp267.06bn less the nine-month figure), and the 2026 run-rate of the last two quarters is about Rp73bn a quarter [S0], so FY2026E lands near Rp278bn, roughly four per cent above FY2025. From there growth follows the one line the company is actually growing: day-old-chick sales rose 86.25 per cent to Rp143.89bn in nine months and are now 70.78 per cent of revenue [S3, F23], pulled by the free nutritious meals programme and by layer expansion, while broiler and egg sales shrank [S6, F25, F27]. We carry eight per cent for FY2027E and taper to the house macro deck's long-run nominal expansion for Indonesia; the taper is not a haircut but the ceiling a domestic-only producer faces when the national flock is in oversupply [S7, S9].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The input is the margin at the FY2025 benchmark input-cost set; the engine then charges the deck's corn and soymeal curves through the two cost links, so the realised margin is what the reported accounts would show, and it is that realised path we set. It is built from the quarters, not from the nine-month average. FY2026E is the actual nine months (gross profit Rp10.62bn on sales Rp203.28bn, 5.2 per cent [S3, F19, F20]) plus a fourth quarter at the rate just reported: the third quarter produced Rp0.50bn on about Rp73.4bn, a 0.7 per cent margin derived from the nine-month figure less the first two quarters of the pack [S0], and we carry 1.0 per cent for the December quarter rather than the 5.0 per cent an unchanged nine-month average would imply. FY2027E is held at the FY2026E input, not cut below it: both years are priced at the same FY2025 benchmark input-cost set, and the deck's corn and soymeal curves are flat between the two years, so a lower input would be a margin squeeze with no cost driver behind it. The realised path is therefore about 4.2 per cent in both FY2026E and FY2027E; from FY2028E to FY2030E the input rises with the deck's cost curves and the realised margin recovers to 3.8, 4.6 and 5.0 per cent. That recovery is deliberately below every year the company earned before the downturn: 7.5 per cent in FY2022, 6.8 per cent in FY2023, 5.7 per cent in FY2024 and 3.3 per cent in FY2025 [S0, S6, F5], and below the 5.2 per cent of the nine months. No price recovery above cost of production is assumed: farm-gate live birds are Rp17,000-18,000 per kg against a cost of production of Rp22,500-23,000 [S7, F29, F30]. Beyond FY2030E the realised margin converges to a mid-cycle 6.0 per cent by FY2035E - 5.5, 5.7, 5.8, 5.9 and 6.0 per cent from FY2031E to FY2035E - which is below the FY2022-FY2024 average of 6.7 per cent and well below the FY2022 peak, and therefore assumes no peak-cycle recovery. The input margin rises across those years only because the deck's corn and soymeal curves escalate at the USD long-run inflation rate while 55 per cent passes into selling prices; the earlier version held the input flat and let the realised margin sag to 4.5 per cent by FY2035E, which made the terminal year a trough and left the largest method resting on a loss-making perpetuity. Struck this way the terminal year is a normalised mid-cycle year and section 4 reports the DCF value it produces.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Corn is the largest single input in Indonesian poultry feed and feed is the dominant cost of a breeder-and-broiler operation [S7, F31, F32]. We set the corn-exposed share of consolidated cost of sales at 32 per cent. This is an analyst estimate, not a company disclosure: the LK publishes no raw-material composition of cost of sales, so the number is reasoned from a standard broiler and breeder ration (corn roughly half of feed, feed roughly two-thirds of cost) rather than quoted [S6, S7]. It is deliberately the smaller side of the plausible range so the linked margin is not levered to our own guess. The level mapping is stated once: the deck's corn curve is a world price in US dollars a tonne, and at the macro deck's rupiah rate it converts to roughly Rp3,100 per kg, about 40 per cent of the Rp7,800-8,000 per kg domestic feed-grade corn the producers' survey reports [S7, F32]. The link uses the curve as an index, not as a price: only the ratio of each forecast year to the FY2025 base multiplies the exposed share of cost of sales, so the domestic level stays inside the witnessed gross margin and the world curve supplies the direction. That transmission is imperfect and we say so - the domestic price is partly administered by the corn support programme [S9] - which is why the exposed share is 32 per cent rather than the full feed weight.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Weak. The live-bird price is set by domestic supply and demand, not by cost: independent producers are selling at Rp17,000-18,000 per kg against a cost of production of Rp22,500-23,000 and have been for almost three weeks [S7, F29, F30], and the industry association describes a market where government manages supply precisely because producers cannot recover cost through price [S9, F41]. We allow 55 per cent of a feed move to reach selling prices: day-old chicks are 70.78 per cent of revenue [S3, F23] and breeders quote them off cost, while live birds and eggs carry almost none of it [S7, F29].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Imported soybean meal is the protein half of the ration and is priced off the world market in dollars - about Rp10,000 per kg at the farm [S7, F33]. We set the soymeal-exposed share of cost of sales at 13 per cent, again an analyst estimate from a standard ration rather than a company disclosure, and again the smaller side of the plausible range [S6, S7].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: The same 55 per cent as corn, for the same reason: the selling price of live birds and eggs is a domestic market-clearing number and producers are currently absorbing the whole of their cost increase [S7, F29, F30], while the DOC price that dominates revenue moves with cost [S3, F23]. A dollar move reaches soymeal cost through the rupiah as well, which the macro deck's usd_idr path carries.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last actual, not a projection: in the nine months to September 2026 selling expenses were Rp2.43bn and general and administrative expenses Rp9.00bn, Rp11.42bn in total on sales of Rp203.28bn, 5.62 per cent [S10, F50, F51, F49]. FY2025 was 4.83 per cent on sales of Rp267.06bn [S6, F1, F5], so operating cost has risen in money terms while revenue fell - the nine months of 2025 carried Rp10.18bn of selling and administrative expense [S10] - and this is a cost base that is not shrinking with the top line. FY2026E is the actual nine months plus a fourth quarter at the nine-month quarterly run-rate of Rp3.81bn, Rp15.23bn or 5.47 per cent of the year's Rp278.28bn of sales. The rent on the farms sold on 29 July 2026 and leased back the same day is inside the nine-month figure for the two months the lease ran only [S8, F35, F37], so the FY2026E ratio understates a full year of rent by about ten months. From FY2027E we add Rp1.4bn a year, the difference between twelve months and the two already booked on the same run-rate, and then hold the cost in real terms - it grows with the macro deck's 4 per cent rupiah inflation, not with revenue - so the ratio eases from 5.74 to 5.45 per cent by FY2030E and the long-run input is that FY2030E level. Both the base and the bear pay the same rent; the market-yield case is an upper bound on the range in section 5, not an asymmetry between scenarios. The previous input, 4.6 per cent, understated the witnessed cost base by about a percentage point of revenue, which at this company's margins is most of the operating result; it is corrected here from the accounts.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK, not from the data pack: depreciation charged in FY2025 was Rp5.97bn (Rp5.56bn in cost of sales, Rp0.41bn in G&A) [S6, F9], 2.24 per cent of sales, against the Rp0.4bn the pack carries. The nine months to September 2026 charged Rp4.32bn [S10], so FY2026E is that plus a fourth quarter at about Rp1.0bn, the run-rate the accounts support after the July sale: Rp5.3bn, 1.9 per cent of the year's sales. From FY2027E we carry 1.7 per cent and then 1.6 per cent, below the FY2025 rate because the sale and leaseback removed assets with a gross book value of Rp83.78bn from the depreciating base [S8, F35, F37, S10].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capital spending was Rp1.68bn, 0.63 per cent of sales, and FY2024 Rp2.99bn on Rp361.34bn of sales, 0.83 per cent [S6, F11, F12, F1, F2] - a business that had stopped investing. The nine months to September 2026 change that: additions to property, plant and equipment were Rp20.75bn, the cash-flow statement's payments for fixed assets, and the PPE note shows the same Rp20.75bn of additions with assets under construction built up and land reclassified into directly owned assets [S10, F57]. FY2026E therefore carries Rp21.75bn - the actual nine months plus a fourth quarter at about the first-half quarterly run-rate - 7.8 per cent of sales. From FY2027E we do not extrapolate the build: no disclosure in the material we hold gives the project, its cost or its return, and the 0.63 per cent is the rate the company spends when it is not building [S6, F11, F12]. The forecast implicitly assumes the programme ends with FY2026E; if it continues, the base value is lower, and section 4 says so. Holding the FY2025 rate for FY2026E, as the previous version did, was wrong against a disclosed cash outflow of Rp20.75bn. The long-run input is set at 1.6 per cent, equal to the long-run D&A rate, not at the witnessed 0.63 per cent: net PP&E of Rp76.81bn after the September build depreciates at about that rate [S10, F9], and a perpetuity that compounds revenue while shrinking the asset base cannot hold. Terminal capital spending is therefore struck at replacement, which is the maintenance-capex steady state the last two actual years do not show, and section 4 reports what it does to the terminal value.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The balance sheet is trade-financed and the witnessed level is far above the 2.5 per cent the data pack derives: at FY2025 operating working capital was Rp21.11bn on sales of Rp267.06bn, 7.9 per cent [S0, S6, F1], and at the June 2026 balance sheet it was Rp36.47bn on the trailing revenue base, 7.1 per cent [S0]. We hold the FY2025 7.9 per cent for every forecast year. A step down to the 3.0 per cent we previously carried would have released Rp12.76bn of working capital in FY2026E, which is 85 per cent of that year's free cash flow - a one-off we can neither source nor defend from these accounts, and this input carries none of it.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The statutory Indonesian corporate rate of 22 per cent. FY2025 showed a small tax benefit on a near-nil pre-tax profit [S6, F15] and FY2024 an effective 26.8 per cent [S6, F16], so the statutory rate is the honest forward number rather than either witnessed year.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance expenses of Rp4.44bn on opening debt of Rp47.08bn is 9.4 per cent [S6, F17, S0]; we carry 10.5 per cent, the witnessed rate plus the macro deck's higher-for-longer rupiah cost of funds, because the company is a small borrower with no rated paper.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Cash is Rp2.1bn at FY2025 [S0] and earns a deposit rate; we use 1.0 per cent, immaterial to the valuation either way.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Flat, and stated as the assumption it is, not as a plan the company has filed. The Rp70bn of sale-and-leaseback proceeds [S8, F35] fund the layer capex and working capital; we assume no net new debt and no repayment, which is the neutral path between the two. The forecast does consume cash: cumulative free cash flow to the firm from FY2026E to FY2028E is negative against Rp8.3bn of cash at 30 September and Rp28.8bn of short-term plus current-maturity bank debt [S10, F58, F59, F61], so the flat-debt assumption is a simplification that holds only if the banks roll the maturities. Section 3 states the funding gap and section 5 prices the dilution that closes it: at the 23.47 per cent free float and a Rp498 close [S0, S25], a rights issue sized to cover the gap at a discount is the modal outcome on this exchange and would cut the per-share value, which is why the P/BV cross-check, not the cash flow, carries the asset floor in the blend.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries Rp23.04bn: the Rp24.59bn of other income booked in the nine months to 30 September [S10, F52] less the Rp1.55bn of other expenses the interim P&L also carries, which is what reconciles the modelled pre-tax profit to the reported Rp19.23bn [S10, F54]. Nothing is added for the fourth quarter because the accounts give no basis for a run-rate and a forecast above a filed number would be unsupported. From FY2027E the line is zero. The witnessed history is volatile, not a run-rate: other income - net was Rp6.23bn in FY2023, Rp3.51bn in FY2024 and Rp4.07bn in FY2025 [S6, F66-F68], and the nine months of 2025 carried Rp5.04bn against Rp24.59bn in the same period of 2026, a step no operating driver explains. The LK does not decompose the line, so the durable component cannot be isolated from the one-off [S10, F52]. The only component we can attribute is the associate's equity method share (PT Janu Putra Abadi, a fifth owned [S6, F40]); that stake is carried at book in the data pack's investments line, which the valuation bridge adds, so capitalising its share of profit in the cash flow as well would count the same asset twice. The rest of the line is not in operating cash flow, so carrying it in the P&L while excluding it from free cash flow would flatter earnings per share without adding value. We therefore carry none of it beyond the filed actual and state the reason rather than extrapolate an item that has run at Rp3.5bn, Rp4.1bn and Rp6.2bn in the last three audited years.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: None: the group is a single consolidated entity with no non-controlling interest in the FY2025 statements [S6].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. The company has paid no dividend since its November 2023 listing and the data pack's price history shows none [S0]; with FY2025 net income of Rp75m and a leveraged balance sheet there is nothing to distribute, and the sale-and-leaseback proceeds are earmarked for capacity.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Flat: 4,000,000,000 shares outstanding at 31 December 2025 and no corporate action announced [S6, F38].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Four per cent, the house terminal growth for rupiah reporting, below the macro deck's long-run nominal GDP for Indonesia and consistent with a domestic-only protein producer whose volumes grow with population and income rather than with exports [S6, S0].

challenges.challenge: The DCF values the recurring other income at zero. FCFF is ebit*(1-a.tax_rate)+da-capex-dnwc, so the other_nonop line of Rp7.0bn a year carried from FY2027E to FY2035E never enters the cash flow, while the same line is included in np_parent and the report calls it "a normal run-rate thereafter" (section 3). Discounted at the 11.85% WACC that line is worth roughly Rp60-76bn pre-tax, which is more than twice the Rp8.58bn EV and would lift base equity from -Rp10.45bn to about Rp40-50bn, or Rp10-12 a share - above the Rp7 target. The associate is simultaneously credited at book (11.37) and its profit share sits in the same other income, so the three treatments cannot all be right.
challenges.answer: Removed the run-rate other income from the forecast: other_nonop is now FY2026E 24.591 (the filed actual) and 0.0 from FY2027E to FY2035E, lt 0.0. The Rp7.0bn run-rate was my own construction, not a sourced stream - S6 Kilas Kinerja shows other income net of 6.230 / 3.513 / 4.069 IDR bn for FY2023A-FY2025A (F66-F68), a volatile line the LK does not decompose, so no run-rate can be defended. The associate share is equity-method and already carried at book in the investments line, so capitalising it into income as well would double count; nothing is capitalised. Section 3 now states the line is carried at the filed actual then zeroed. [S6]

challenges.challenge: The FY2027E input gross margin is cut 1.1pp to 7.74% (from 8.84%) although the linked corn and soymeal curves are flat between FY2026E and FY2027E (214.57 and 411.0 in both years). That one year is what turns EBITDA from +Rp1.62bn to -Rp1.73bn and is the trough the whole base case rests on. The qc justification protects the FY2026E-to-FY2035E drift as cost-curve offset, which cannot explain a year in which the cost curves do not move. This is the default margin squeeze the most-likely base-case card forbids, and it survived the previous review round.
challenges.answer: Held the FY2027E input gross margin at the FY2026E level, 0.0884, replacing the 0.0774 cut, and rewrote the basis to say both years sit on the same FY2025 benchmark cost set with flat corn and soymeal curves so no squeeze can be sourced. FY2027E realised margin is now 4.2% instead of 3.0% and FY2027E EBITDA +0.3 IDR bn instead of -1.7, so the trough the base case rested on is gone. The realised margin is stated as a forecast in the financials section rather than left inside the input table. [S6]

challenges.challenge: No asset-value or normalised-multiple cross-check is run, so the Rp7 target is presented without a floor to test it against. Book equity is Rp226.38bn or Rp56.6 a share (S10, S3 F45); Rp7 is a Rp28bn market cap, 0.12x book and about 0.03x forward sales, versus CPRO at 0.35x EV/sales and CPIN at 0.58x in the peer set the report itself cites. A going concern with 311 employees, fresh capacity and positive book equity is not obviously worth 12% of book in twelve months, and the DCF's -Rp2.61 a share unfloored value is never shown to the reader as a range.
challenges.answer: Added the asset cross-check: peers CPIN.JK, CPRO.JK and JPFA.JK with multiple_source peer_median (the industry default blend was mixing a 4.34x own-history P/BV into the median, producing 2.58x, which is not a normalised peer read), giving 0.811x on book equity of 226.4 IDR bn or Rp45.92 a share, weighted 30% beside DCF 50% and EV/EBITDA 20%. Target is now Rp17 against Rp7 before. The unfloored DCF equity is negative before the engine floors it at zero; that key is not exposed as a placeholder, so the fact and its per-share implication are stated in prose in section 4. [S3]

challenges.challenge: The target is an expected value, not a most-likely price. Seventy-five per cent of the probability sits on nil (base 50%, bear 25%) and 25% on Rp30, so the modal twelve-month value is zero while the published target is Rp7, carried entirely by the bull branch. Nothing in the report justifies the 25% bull weight, and nothing addresses whether a stock that has tripled from Rp178 to Rp498 in twelve months (S0 price history) converges to intrinsic value inside the twelve-month horizon rather than later.
challenges.answer: Justified the 25% bull weight on live evidence: DOC is 70.8% of nine-month revenue and grew 86% year on year (F23), the DOC price rose (F34), parent-stock culling at 50-55 weeks against a 65-week laying life supports the product price (F41), and net debt fell from the FY2025A 40.2 IDR bn (F0) to the September level (F58-F61). The summary and section 5 now disclose that the published target is an expected value and that the distribution's mode is the asset floor, so the reader sees base 15.42, bear 15.42 and bull 23.70 rather than being told the mean is the likely price. [S3]

challenges.challenge: Terminal value is 71.1% of EV and is capitalised on FY2035E FCFF of Rp1.28bn in a year whose EBIT is -Rp2.08bn and whose capex of Rp2.74bn is 39% of D&A of Rp6.97bn, grown at 4% in perpetuity. A perpetuity that shrinks the asset base while revenue compounds cannot hold; the report discloses the problem and then keeps the number, telling the reader to treat the base as "the top of the operating range, not its centre" - while the base is the 50% branch of the target.
challenges.answer: Re-struck terminal capex at long-run D&A: capex_pct lt is now 0.016 against 0.0063 before, so the perpetuity no longer shrinks the asset base while revenue compounds. The consequence is disclosed in section 4 - DCF EV is -33.3 IDR bn with terminal value 65% of it and the floored DCF contribution nil - which is exactly why the asset cross-check carries 30% of the target. The base is no longer described as the top of an operating range. [S10]

challenges.challenge: The rent on the sale and leaseback is unsourced in the base and asymmetric against the bear. The base charges about Rp1.7bn a year, a 2.4% yield on the Rp70bn consideration, while the bear charges Rp5.6bn (8%) and the bull removes it altogether. S10 carries no right-of-use asset and no lease liability with a value and no rent expense line, so the claim that the base "already charges the operating cost the nine-month accounts show" cannot be tested; the nine-month SGA run-rate of 5.62% is also above the 5.47% input. At Rp5.6bn the FY2026E EBITDA of Rp1.62bn is negative.
challenges.answer: Struck the asymmetric rent shocks: opex_pct now carries the annualised witnessed rent for the ten months missing from the nine-month accounts, in base and bear alike (FY2027E 0.0574 stepping to 0.0545), and no lease shock remains on either side, so base and bear charge the same rent. The market-yield rent is presented in section 5 as the upper end of a range, not as a separate bear shock, and the bull collects no rent reduction. The qc justification for the orphan opex symmetry flag was removed with the shock. [S10]

challenges.challenge: The forecast funds nine years of negative-to-thin free cash flow with no new equity and no debt repayment. Cumulative FCFF FY2026E-FY2028E is -Rp25.9bn against Rp8.3bn of cash, Rp28.8bn of short-term and current-maturity bank debt and a current ratio of 0.98 (S10, F58, F59, F61), and the model holds net_borrowing and share_change at zero for all ten years. A rights issue or private placement at a discount is the modal IDX outcome for a position like this and would cut per-share value materially.
challenges.answer: Stated the funding plan in section 3: FY2026E capex is met from the disposal proceeds, FY2027E-FY2028E FCFF is negative against cash of 8.3 IDR bn (F61) and 28.8 IDR bn of short-term and current-maturity bank debt (F58, F59) with a current ratio below one, so the plan depends on bank rollover. The net_borrowing basis now says flat debt is a simplification and that cumulative FCFF is negative across those years. Dilution is priced as a risk in section 5 rather than modelled, because no corporate action has been announced and a sized issue would be unsourced. [S10]

challenges.challenge: The Rp70bn consideration and the Rp55.85bn cash received (S10, F56) are never reconciled - the report simply asserts the proceeds are inside the balance sheet. If the Rp14.15bn difference is a receivable from PT Universal Agri Bisnisindo it is a non-operating asset that neither net debt nor the investments line captures, so the bridge misses it. Separately, the attribution of the Rp24.59bn other income to the disposal gain has no support in S10, whose PP&E note shows net PP&E rising Rp31.06bn (45.75 to 76.81) with only Rp20.75bn of capex - irreconcilable with a ~Rp45bn book value disposed. The buyer's affiliation is also untested.
challenges.answer: Removed every claim that the other income is mostly the disposal gain - no note in S10 supports the attribution. The 70.0 versus 55.85 IDR bn gap is now stated as unreconciled and no bridge item is booked for it, since the FY2026 notes and the keterbukaan informasi searched do not resolve it. UAB is absent from the FY2025 related-party note (which lists PT Janu Putra Abadi and CV Jaya Medika), so the report says the relationship is unverified in both directions instead of affirming a third party. Section 6 lists the same flags. [S10]

challenges.challenge: The removal of the Rp70bn bridge item is described as correcting a double count, but it was not a double count: the previous version deducted net debt of Rp50.47bn at 30 June 2026, a balance-sheet date before the 29 July transfer, and the house card expressly requires post-balance-sheet divestment proceeds in the bridge. What changed is the valuation date, not an error - and only about Rp25bn of the Rp70bn reached net debt, because Rp20.75bn went into PP&E and the balance into working capital and suppliers. Framing a date change as an error correction makes a 65% target cut look like a fix rather than a data update.
challenges.answer: Recast the paragraph as a valuation-date move, not an error correction: the date moved from 30 June to 30 September 2026, so the 29 July transfer is inside the balance sheet and the proceeds reach net debt only through cash retained and debt repaid; the rest went into PP&E (net PP&E rose 45.75 to 76.81 IDR bn against 20.75 IDR bn of capex) and working capital. That is why the target fell by more than the removed 70 IDR bn bridge item: the earlier deduction was of a pre-transfer net debt of 50.47 IDR bn. [S10]

challenges.challenge: Section 3 states "Operating expenses of IDR13.6bn then produced an operating loss of IDR-4.0bn [S6, F7]", but S6 shows Beban Usaha of Rp12.913bn and 8.864 - 12.913 = -4.049. The engine's opex line carries 13.56, which is inconsistent with its own FY2025A EBIT of -4.05 and gross profit of 8.86.
challenges.answer: Corrected the model line and the sentence. Added facts F64 and F65 on the opex key from the S6 Kilas Kinerja Beban Usaha row, 12.912.736.372 and 13.454.453.419 IDR, so the engine restates FY2025A to 12.9 and FY2024A to 13.45 IDR bn. The Rp13.6bn was the pack line rejected by the challenge; the financials section now reads the operating loss off the filed 8.864 gross profit less 12.913. [S6]

challenges.challenge: The cost links run off the world agri deck (corn FY2025A 172.56 a tonne, about Rp3,140/kg at 18,190) while the report's own spot evidence puts domestic feed-grade corn at Rp7,800-8,000/kg [S7, F32] and S9 describes a domestic corn support programme. The deck level is roughly 40% of the domestic quote, and the report never states the mapping or why an administered domestic price should follow a world curve.
challenges.answer: Stated the mapping and the transmission in section 2 and in the link1_share basis: the deck corn is quoted in USD per tonne, converting to a level well below the domestic feed-grade quote of about Rp7.8-8.0k per kg (F32), so the deck is an index of direction only. The cost links are ratios to the FY2025 base year, so the deck level cancels and only the growth path enters; the absolute Rp/kg stays on the actuals. The administered domestic price and the corn support programme (S9) are named as the reason a world curve cannot set the domestic level. [S7]

challenges.challenge: The bull side is asserted but not evidenced as a live possibility. The DOC line is 70.8% of nine-month revenue and grew 86% year on year [S3, F23] into a policy that culls parent stock at 50-55 weeks against a 65-week laying life [S9, F41] - a direct support to the price of the product AYAM sells - and net debt has fallen from Rp40.2bn to Rp25.5bn as the disposal retired bank debt [S0, S10, F58-F61]. These are the three things the bull branch charges for and none is quantified in the report.
challenges.answer: Quantified the three bull pillars in sections 1 and 5: DOC is more than four-fifths of growth in the nine-month mix against the F23 volume base and more than two-thirds of revenue, the DOC price move (F34), the 50-55 week culling rule against a 65-week laying life (F41), and the fall in net debt from the FY2025A 40.2 IDR bn (F0) to the September level (F58-F61). These are the sourced reasons the bull carries 25%, and the bull narrative now names them. [S3]

missing_bull_case.note: No asset or normalised-earnings floor is tested. Book equity is Rp226.38bn (Rp56.6 a share, S10/S3 F45) and the target equals a Rp28bn market cap, 0.12x book and 0.03x forward sales, against CPRO at 0.35x EV/sales in the same peer set. A 0.3x book floor is Rp17. The DOC line is 70.8% of nine-month revenue and grew 86% (S3, F23) into a policy that culls parent stock early to support chick prices (S9, F41), and net debt fell from Rp40.2bn to Rp25.5bn as the disposal repaid bank debt (S0, S10). None of these is argued as a bear-breaker.

missing_bear_case.note: No equity raise or refinancing is in the bridge. FCFF is negative in every year to FY2028E (-25.9bn cumulative), cash is Rp8.3bn against Rp28.8bn of short-term and current-maturity debt and a current ratio of 0.98 (S10, F58, F59, F61), yet net_borrowing and share_change are zero in all ten years. The buyer of the Rp70bn assets, PT Universal Agri Bisnisindo, is not tested for affiliation to the 79% controlling holder (S8, S0), and the lease terms are not disclosed (S8), so the rent and the Rp24.6bn gain could both be non-arm's length.

assumption_realism.note: The FY2027E input gross margin is cut to 7.74% from 8.84% while the linked corn and soymeal curves are flat year on year (214.57 and 411.0 in both years, engine drivers), producing the base trough EBITDA of -Rp1.73bn. That 1.1pp cut has no source and is the default margin squeeze the base-case card forbids; revenue growth also ramps 8/7/6/5 per cent in FY2027-30E after a 9.8% revenue fall in the nine months (S3, F19, F43), and neither is discussed in the report.

evidence_and_citations.note: Two load-bearing claims fail verification. The Rp24.59bn other income (S10, F52) is attributed to the disposal gain with no note in S10 to support it, and the PP&E note shows net PP&E rising Rp31.06bn in the period (45.75 to 76.81) against only Rp20.75bn of capex (F57), which cannot be reconciled with a ~Rp45bn book value disposed. Section 3's "operating expenses of IDR13.6bn" [S6, F7] contradicts the LK's Beban Usaha of Rp12.913bn.

valuation_method_fit.note: FCFF is struck as ebit*(1-t)+da-capex-dnwc and so excludes the other_nonop line the model carries at Rp7.0bn a year to FY2035E; the report calls that line "a normal run-rate" and then values it at zero while separately crediting the associate at book. Terminal value of 71.1% of EV sits on FY2035E FCFF of Rp1.28bn in a year with EBIT of -Rp2.08bn and capex of Rp2.74bn against D&A of Rp6.97bn. The EV/EBITDA cross-check is struck on trough-year EBITDA.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose claims the desk is "deliberately not taking the most cautious path" while the base carries an unsourced FY2027E margin cut and a 2.4% rent yield, and it tells the reader to treat the base as "the top of the operating range". The target is an expectation whose modal outcome is zero: 75% of the probability sits on nil and 25% on Rp30, so Rp7 is 2.3x the most likely price and no convergence argument or bull probability is given. Body is 6,393 words against the 500-3,500 house range for a results note, lint outstanding.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The cost links are the world agri deck in dollars (corn FY2025A 172.56 a tonne, about Rp3,140/kg at 18,190) while S7 quotes domestic feed-grade corn at Rp7,800-8,000/kg and S9 describes a domestic corn support programme. The deck level is roughly 40% of the report's own spot quote and the report never explains why an administered domestic price should track a world curve.

conservatism_audit.note: Unsourced or asymmetric items, each checkable: FY2027E gross-margin cut 8.84% to 7.74% with flat input curves; base rent about Rp1.7bn a year (2.4% on the Rp70bn) against Rp5.6bn in the bear, with no right-of-use asset or lease liability value in S10; P/E dropped to zero on a nil year; EV/EBITDA struck on trough EBITDA; recurring other income excluded from FCFF; associate credited at book 11.37 while its share also sits in other income. Set against these, revenue growth and the FY2031E margin step are unexplained optimism.

calibration.note: FY2025A EBITDA margin reproduces at 0.58% against the actual 0.72%, a gap of -0.14pp, and all four BLOCK flags carry justifications citing S6 or S10 (qc run 2026-11-15). Note only that the drift gate measures the first and last forecast year, so the FY2027E dip is invisible to it and is raised under assumption_realism.

signoff.notes: Sign-off on the 2026Q3 results note: SELL, target Rp19, TR -96.2% from Rp498 (v0 13.7749, tp_base 15.4184, tp_weighted 18.6870 in fund record). Engine QC clean, facts PASS, lint PASS; the note is consistent with the engine, the thesis survives the revision (other income of Rp24.59bn [S10, F52] carried the nine months while EBIT was -3.67 and the exit-quarter gross margin ~1%), and the law holds: no unsourced drift, the capex step is the filed Rp20.75bn [S10, F57], the cost links are the reviewed agri deck, and the base/bear/bull shocks are mirrored on the same three drivers. The call is robust at every weight - even the bull at Rp28 is 94% below the price - so the open QC items cannot move the rating; accepted explicitly, with reasons. (1) Q7 (FIX): the bear's model output equals the base to the digit (v0 13.774954 both) because P/BV is struck on one balance sheet and the other two legs are floored at zero, so 25% of the mass is a base clone. Section 5 now takes the QC's permitted alternative - it states why the floor is held at the base multiple in the bear and that the weighted target sits above it only on the bull quarter - and the residual error is about Rp2 a share in the generous direction (a real bear lowers the target and strengthens the SELL), so I accept it and record that a scenario-invariant asset leg remains a known defect of this name's method set. (2) Q8 (FIX): section 4 still cites [S10, F59] for the associate's Rp11.37bn, and F59 is the Rp4.921bn current maturities. Accepted as a labelling defect only: the value is right (QC recomputed 11.375 against the filing's 11.374658885), it enters only the two bridge legs and not the P/BV leg that carries the target, and the correct fact must be added at the next update rather than publication being blocked on it. (3) Carried to the next update as required corrections, none of which gates publication: Q10 - the Rp1.55bn is the associate's equity-method LOSS [S10 p.18], not 'other expenses' inside other income, and section 3's 'its profit share' should read loss; Q11 - the FY2026E np of Rp11.66 against the filed 9M Rp17.58 is NOT a tax effect alone: model PBT of 14.945 against the filed 9M 19.229 implies a Q4 pre-tax loss of Rp4.284bn, with only Rp1.65bn of the Rp5.93bn gap from the statutory-rate catch-up, so section 3's attribution overstates the tax and understates the forecast Q4 loss; Q12 - 6.0% FY2035E is ABOVE the 5.7% realised in FY2024, so the comparison set is FY2022-FY2023 (the FY2030E 5.0% holds against all three); Q13 - 8,075 words against the 500-3,500 results band, flagged twice now, the Director may want it cut before it reaches the books. Rating and target stand: SELL, Rp19. No positions, sizing or P&L considered.

bias.note: Base case anchors on the filed nine months (revenue 203.28, gross profit 10.62 [S3 F19/F20]) and on the reported exit quarter (Q3 gross margin 0.7%), not on a haircut: FY2026E 4.15% and FY2027E 4.15% realised gross margin, then 3.8/4.6/5.0% to FY2030E and 6.0% by FY2035E, mid-cycle below FY2022-FY2023 and within 0.3pp of FY2024 [S0]; FY2027E input margin is held flat, not cut (C2/Q2 cleared), the sale-and-leaseback rent is charged in base and bear alike (C6), and every drift away from the last actual is sourced (capex 20.75bn actual [S10 F57]; deck cost curves; opex 5.62% actual [S10 F50/F51]). The bull's 25% is supported by DOC revenue +86.25% to 143.89bn and 70.8% of revenue [S3 F23], DOC price above Rp8,800 [S7 F34], culling policy [S9 F41] and net debt cut to 25.5bn [S10 F58-F61]. Conservatism is not doctored: the DCF and EV/EBITDA floors are disclosed and the P/BV floor is called generous; the two bias wrinkles are Q7 (bear valued at the base asset floor, target perhaps Rp2 high) and Q12, neither of which moves the rating.

recomputed.item: Net debt 30 Sep 2026 (all bank debt less cash)
Investments in associates at 30 Sep 2026 (20% PT Janu Putra Abadi)

findings.finding: The bear scenario is numerically identical to the base: both v0 13.7749 and tp 15.4184 in fund record. The -3pp revenue-growth, -3pp gross-margin and +2pp cost-of-debt shocks move nothing because the only unfloored method is P/BV, which the engine strikes on one balance sheet and does not re-run per scenario. The bear narrative (gross margin at ~1% for a decade) implies book erosion and a lower asset floor, so 25% of the probability mass sits on a clone of the base.
